skill.name: intercom-automation
skill.description: Automate Intercom support workflows through Rube MCP, including conversations, contacts, companies, segments, admins, and schema discovery.
skill.summary: Guide Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Intercom automation using Rube MCP tool workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static command and reconnaissance detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, API parameter names, and Intercom entity identifiers. The only substantive risk found is that documented write workflows can send customer-visible replies or alter Intercom records without explicit confirmation guidance.

remediation.issue: Mutable Intercom operations can affect customers or support records.
remediation.suggestion: Add a required confirmation step before create, reply, assign, close, reopen, or detach operations.

remediation.issue: Duplicate sends are possible on retry or timeout.
remediation.suggestion: Document a message ID or conversation-state check before retrying conversation creation or replies.

remediation.issue: External OAuth and MCP handling are required for Intercom access.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend least-privilege Intercom scopes and describe which data is handled by Rube MCP.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Intercom connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `intercom`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
- `from`: Object with `type` ('user'/'lead') and `id` for conversation creator
- CREATE_CONVERSATION requires a contact (user/lead) as the `from` field, not an admin

- Conversation bodies support HTML; plain text is auto-wrapped in `

` tags
- `admin_id`: Admin ID for replies from admin, assignment, and close/reopen
- `assignee_id`: Admin or team ID for assignment
- `admin_id` is REQUIRED for admin replies, close, reopen, and assignment operations
- Internal notes use `message_type: 'note'`; visible only to workspace members
- SEARCH_CONTACTS uses structured query filters, not free-text; format: `{field, operator, value}`
- LIST_CONTACTS returns paginated results; use `starting_after` cursor for pagination
- Teams appear in the admins list with `type: 'team'`
- Pass cursor in `pagination.starting_after` for next page
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Closing requires an admin_id and optional body message
**Supported fields for contacts**: email, name, role, created_at, updated_at, signed_up_at, last_see
3. Use admin.id for replies, assignments, and state changes
| Reply to conversation | INTERCOM_REPLY_TO_CONVERSATION | conversation_id, body, admin_id |
| Assign conversation | INTERCOM_ASSIGN_CONVERSATION | conversation_id, admin_id, assignee_id |
| Contact by external ID | INTERCOM_SHOW_CONTACT_BY_EXTERNAL_ID | external_id |

semantic_findings.title: Customer-Impacting Intercom Actions Lack Confirmation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The workflow documents replies, assignment, close, reopen, and contact-company detach operations but does not require an explicit confirmation gate before mutable Intercom actions. Misuse could send customer-visible messages or alter support records.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited workflows explicitly include write actions and note duplicate-send risk. The concern is operational misuse rather than malicious code, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Intercom work often requires precise tool schemas, admin IDs, and pagination rules. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP workflows for safer support automation.
actual_capabilities: Guides setup for Rube MCP and Intercom OAuth connection.
Maps tool sequences for conversations, replies, assignment, close, and reopen workflows.
Documents contact, admin, team, segment, company, and count lookup flows.
Explains structured search filters, pagination cursors, and admin ID resolution.
Lists known pitfalls for HTML bodies, duplicate sends, rate limits, and required IDs.
limitations: Requires a connected Rube MCP server and active Intercom OAuth connection.
Does not include executable automation scripts or direct API clients.
Depends on current Rube tool schemas, so users must search tools before calls.
Can modify Intercom data when used with write-capable tools.

use_cases.title: Route Active Support Conversations
use_cases.description: Find conversations, resolve admin IDs, and assign work to the correct teammate or team.

use_cases.title: Investigate Customer Records
use_cases.description: Search contacts, view segments, inspect company relationships, and gather context before taking action.

use_cases.title: Build Repeatable Intercom Procedures
use_cases.description: Create standard prompts for replies, pagination, counts, and workflow checks using current Rube schemas.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Intercom Connection
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Intercom automation skill to verify that Rube MCP is connected. Search current tools first, check the Intercom connection status, and tell me what is ready or missing.

prompt_templates.title: Find A Customer Conversation
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Intercom for conversations related to this customer: [customer details]. Use current Rube tool schemas, explain the filters used, and summarize the matching conversations.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare A Safe Reply
prompt_templates.prompt: Review conversation [conversation ID], identify the needed admin ID, draft a reply, and stop for my confirmation before sending anything to Intercom.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Segment Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Intercom tools through Rube MCP to inspect segment membership and related company context for [account]. Handle pagination, note approximate counts, and flag any action that would change data.

output_examples.input: Find open conversations for a customer email and suggest the next step.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports the search filters used, lists matching conversation summaries, identifies the assigned admin or team, and recommends a next action.

output_examples.input: Prepare a close message for a resolved conversation.
output_examples.output: The assistant fetches the conversation state, resolves the admin ID, drafts the customer-visible message, and waits for approval before closing.

output_examples.input: Review contact segments and company links for an account.
output_examples.output: The assistant summarizes contact identity, attached segments, company relationships, pagination status, and any limits in the returned data.

best_practices: Search Rube tools first so parameters match the current Intercom schema.
Confirm admin IDs and conversation state before replies, assignment, close, or reopen actions.
Review customer-visible text and record-changing operations before submitting tool calls.
anti_patterns: Retrying replies or conversation creation without checking for duplicate sends.
Using free-text assumptions when Intercom search requires structured filters.
Changing assignments, closing conversations, or detaching contacts without explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill connect directly to Intercom?
faq.answer: No. It guides calls through Rube MCP and requires an active Intercom OAuth connection.

faq.question: Why should tools be searched first?
faq.answer: Rube tool schemas can change. Searching first helps the assistant use current names and parameters.

faq.question: Can it send customer-visible replies?
faq.answer: Yes, when connected tools allow replies. Review and confirm message text before sending.

faq.question: Does it support contact and company lookup?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents contact search, external ID lookup, segment lookup, company listing, and company segment checks.

faq.question: Can it prevent duplicate messages?
faq.answer: It warns about duplicate sends and recommends idempotency checks, but enforcement depends on the workflow using it.

faq.question: Is this skill only for support teams?
faq.answer: No. Support agents, operations managers, and automation engineers can use it for Intercom workflows.
